parameters.content:
## I.LPRD — LP report 136 "Marketing Sub Source Cost Analysis 2" (thin transport ONLY)

Gmail → keep every **`.csv`** attachment → POST the CSV **text** → LP-MCP.
ZERO parsing here: every parse / validate / write rule lives in LP-MCP (fail-closed).
LP schedules this email ~6:45 ET daily · scope **YTD** · feeds Marketing cost, cost per lead.

**CSV CUTOVER (2026-08-10).** This workflow was half-migrated. The Gmail trigger
had moved to CSV while the Code node still routed on the PDF-era filename ID
`_136_` and the HTTP node still posted binary to the PDF route. LP's CSV
attachments are named `_<YYMMDDHHMMSS>_Export.csv` and carry no report id, so
that test could never match — every attachment was dropped and the workflow
completed having done nothing. **No 136 ingest ran between 2026-08-06 and this
fix.**

**⚠️ A DRAFT IS NOT A DEPLOY.** Before this fix, this workflow carried an
unpublished draft from 2026-08-10 17:52 while still RUNNING the 2026-08-06
version (`versionId` != `activeVersionId`). n8n executes the PUBLISHED version.
After editing, publish — or the change is invisible to production.

**Routing is by HEADER now, not filename.** LP-MCP's `detectReportFromHeader`
fingerprints the file and ingests as the resolved type; the slug in the URL is
only a hint, and a mis-slugged file still lands correctly. Scope comes from the
Gmail subject query.

**The body is raw TEXT, not binary.** n8n's binary body mode sends multipart and
overrides Content-Type, which the route rejects with 400 "POST the CSV text as
the request body". The Code node decodes to `json.csv_text`; the HTTP node posts
it raw as `text/csv`.

**Node names still say "PDF".** Deliberate: `connections` reference nodes by
name, and I.LPRB carries the same stale names after the same cutover.

**A Gmail polling trigger cannot backfill.** Forward-only, dedupes on message ID.
Use a direct POST with `?source=manual-backfill` for history.

**Failure handling.** 200 + `success:false` = deterministic rejection — never
retried; logged in `scorecard_ingest_log` + GroupMe. 5xx = transport error —
retried 3×, then reported to `/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`.

**Both outcomes now report (2026-08-29).** The IF's FALSE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`; its TRUE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_succeeded`. TRUE used to dead-end, so a SUCCESSFUL 136
ingest emitted no event at all — the same blind spot that let report 133 read as
broken for eight days after it was fixed.

**⚠️ This telemetry row shares a report_type with the parser.** Unlike 133 (where
telemetry lands under `jobs_by_status` and the parser writes `job_status_ytd`),
`source-cost` maps to `source_cost` on BOTH sides, so every successful run writes
TWO rows to `scorecard_ingest_log`. Tell them apart by `source` (`n8n_telemetry`
vs `n8n`) and by `snapshot_id`, which is null on the telemetry row. Any query
counting successes MUST filter on `source` or it will double-count.
